path.title: APIs and orchestration
path.summary: Pagination, retries, DAGs and explicit failure handling.

lessons.title: Pagination is part of correctness
lessons.summary: Follow every page before declaring an ingestion complete.

blocks.title: The mental model
blocks.body: The API Lab provides a deterministic simulated API on its own local port. Your ingestion Python executes for real only after trusted-Python opt-in. Use the api-paged-customers mission for real request-log checks.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.body: Testing the first page only and assuming the returned count is the total count.

blocks.title: Before you run
blocks.body: What should your loop do when page two is empty but still carries a next cursor?

visual.title: Pagination is part of correctness - visual walkthrough

steps.title: Request page one
steps.body: The first response is often only part of the dataset.

steps.title: Follow the cursor
steps.body: Use the server continuation marker instead of inventing offsets.

steps.title: Persist the batch
steps.body: Track which rows were written successfully.

steps.title: Stop deliberately
steps.body: An absent next cursor ends this traversal; an empty page need not always do so.

lessons.title: Retry safely and deduplicate
lessons.summary: A repeated request must not automatically mean repeated data.

blocks.title: The mental model
blocks.body: The displayed timeline is an authored walkthrough. Real API request logs remain in the API Lab. No OpenTelemetry exporter or external telemetry is activated by Learning.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.body: Retrying every HTTP status forever, or updating the watermark before the batch is committed.

blocks.title: Before you run
blocks.body: What happens when the write succeeded but the acknowledgment was lost?

visual.title: Retry safely and deduplicate - visual walkthrough

steps.title: Transient failure
steps.body: Distinguish a temporary failure from invalid input or an authorization error.

steps.title: Respect backoff
steps.body: Retry only eligible errors and honor the relevant retry policy.

steps.title: Receive duplicates
steps.body: At-least-once delivery can return rows already observed.

steps.title: Commit safely
steps.body: Use a stable business/event key and advance the watermark only after persistence.

lessons.title: Read a DAG as dependencies
lessons.summary: Separate task definitions, scheduler decisions and task outcomes.

blocks.title: The mental model
blocks.body: The diagram is authored for the lesson. Task states become simulation evidence only when the existing Airflow Lab returns a run. A ready task is not necessarily running: resources and scheduling matter.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.body: Assuming every arrow means rows are transported between tasks, or equating dependency order with a guaranteed wall-clock timeline.

blocks.title: Before you run
blocks.body: What blocks load when only transform_a has succeeded?

visual.title: Read a DAG as dependencies - visual walkthrough

steps.title: Read the dependencies
steps.body: Arrows express ordering or data dependencies, not physical data movement.

steps.title: Release ready tasks
steps.body: After extract, both transforms can become ready.

steps.title: Wait at the fan-in
steps.body: Load needs the upstream condition specified by its trigger rule.

steps.title: Inspect the simulator
steps.body: Open Airflow Lab to simulate real authored DAG text safely; it is not an Airflow scheduler.

lessons.title: Retries and trigger rules
lessons.summary: Explain why a cleanup task runs while the pipeline still fails.

blocks.title: The mental model
blocks.body: The diagram explains the dependency structure. Exercise delegates to the existing deterministic Airflow grading engine; learner DAG source is parsed, never executed as arbitrary Python.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.body: Adding all_done to every task and accidentally hiding an upstream failure.

blocks.title: Before you run
blocks.body: How would a watcher task keep the overall failure visible?

visual.title: Retries and trigger rules - visual walkthrough

steps.title: A task fails
steps.body: A retriable failure may transition into a retry wait.

steps.title: Retry budget
steps.body: Retry count and delay determine whether another attempt is allowed.

steps.title: Cleanup
steps.body: all_done requires completion, not success, of upstream tasks.

steps.title: Run outcome
steps.body: A successful cleanup is not proof that the business load succeeded. Inspect the DAG outcome rule.
